doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Music is something you do between meals
summary: He puts family first, calls music something done between meals, and explains why he studied orchestral trumpet.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well you have to kind of jolt people sometimes because you know they’re enthusiastic about what they’re doing but they’re not practical. You know I’m thinking about okay what’s the most important — oh there’s my wife, hello, Miss Patty.

My wife. She’s the greatest. The best. So you know the most important thing is just what we’re doing is your family, your relationship with your closest group, whatever that is. Family, group, you know maybe it’s a singles group. I don’t know. But that’s important.

And maybe this is the right thing. And people always quote me on this, even when I’m not there. Because they realize that it’s true. Music is something you do in between meals. That’s the way I think, every day. Meaning your life is first, your music is part of that, but it’s not the total focus. Because if it is you end up being extraordinary in a not- so-great way sometimes. You know somebody who is walking around, you know they’re just not aware of anything that’s around them, you’re doing a beautiful place and they’re going, “Well you know that rehearsal was too long and I don’t like that conductor.” Well that’s okay if you don’t like him, I can tell you I don’t like the conductor, that’s it. I’m done. You can converse with them a little bit but you can’t rant forever about stuff that — you know and then they end up, that’s why I went to school to study orchestral trumpet. Not jazz. I went to study ‘cause I knew I was weaker in that. And I liked orchestral music. I listen to it all the time you know, as well as some jazz things, as the more I listened. Got more than those first four records, and the radio. The radio was so helpful. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
